data.description:
Speaker file upload fails on the deployed site with **"upload PUT network error"**.
Operator hit this on https://marquee.stage11.dev (2026-08-11) on the Presentation
Upload task. This blocks the file-upload step of the 11-step walkthrough loop —
the competition's evaluation rubric — so treat it as ship-blocking.

## Mechanism (traced, not guessed)

That exact string comes from `src/ui/upload/upload-client.ts:36`:

    xhr.onerror = () => reject(new Error("upload PUT network error"));

`xhr.onerror` fires only on a **browser-level** failure — DNS, TLS, or a blocked
CORS preflight. It does not fire for HTTP error statuses; `xhr.onload` handles
those and produces a different message ("upload PUT failed with status N"). So
the request never reached R2 as far as the browser is concerned.

The upload is a **direct browser PUT to R2**, cross-origin by construction:

- `src/lib/r2/presign.ts` signs against `https://{accountId}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/{bucket}/{key}`
  and deliberately refuses any other host.
- The page origin is `https://marquee.stage11.dev`. Different origin → preflight.
- The PUT is definitively **not** a CORS-simple request: `presignPut` requires
  `content-type` **and** `if-none-match: *`, and `upload-client.ts` attaches an
  `xhr.upload.onprogress` handler. Any one of those forces an `OPTIONS` preflight.
- **There is no CORS configuration anywhere in this repository.** A repo-wide search
  for `cors` / `AllowedOrigins` across `src/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`, and
  `wrangler.jsonc` returns nothing. `wrangler.jsonc` binds the bucket
  (`MEDIA` → `marquee-media`) but a binding does not configure the S3 API's CORS
  rules, which is what a browser PUT is governed by.

Leading hypothesis: **the `marquee-media` bucket has no CORS policy**, so the
preflight is rejected and every browser upload fails. Note the implication —
this likely never worked on the deployed site. The suite is green because nothing
exercises a real cross-origin browser PUT; this is the textbook
"green tests ≠ working product" gap.

Rule out before fixing, in this order: (1) read the bucket's live CORS rules;
(2) check the browser console/network panel for the `OPTIONS` preflight and its
response; (3) only then look at the MRQ-89 bucket-scoped credential — a bad
credential returns **403**, which would surface as "failed with status 403", not
a network error. Do not assume MRQ-89; confirm from the preflight.

## Required outcome

1. **The bucket accepts browser uploads.** Apply a CORS policy to `marquee-media`
   (and the preview bucket if it serves any browser path) that allows `PUT` and
   `OPTIONS` from the site origin, with `content-type` and `if-none-match` in
   `AllowedHeaders` and `etag` exposed. Scope `AllowedOrigins` to the real origins
   — the production domain and whatever local dev origin the team uses. **Do not
   use `*`.**
2. **The policy is in the repo, not just in a dashboard.** A CORS rule that exists
   only as a console click is a rule that silently disappears on the next bucket
   rebuild and that no one can review. Commit the policy as a JSON file plus an
   idempotent apply script (wrangler or the S3 API), and document it in
   `code/platform/cloudflare.md` — see also `docs/` conventions in this repo.
3. **A test that would have caught this.** At minimum, an automated check that
   performs a real cross-origin `OPTIONS` preflight against the bucket and asserts
   the response allows `PUT` from the production origin. It does not belong in the
   45s fast suite — put it in the explicitly-invoked integration suite and wire it
   into the deploy check.
4. **The speaker-facing error stops being developer text.** "upload PUT network
   error" is an internal string in front of the least-equipped person to act on it.
   Replace the user-visible copy with a plain sentence and a retry, per the portal's
   own stated error philosophy (see the comment above `requestJson` in
   `PortalPage.tsx`). Keep the precise string in the console/logs for engineers.

## Constraints

- **Credentials never enter this repo.** It is going public. The apply script reads
  from the environment; the JSON policy file contains no secrets.
- Coordinate with MRQ-89's bucket-scoped credential — if the scoped token lacks the
  permission to *set* CORS, say so in the PR rather than widening the token silently.
- Suite budget 45s (this check goes in the slow suite), gate budget 120s.

## Acceptance

- On the **live deployed site**, signed in as a speaker, a real file uploads to
  completion on the Presentation Upload task — screenshot or recording in the PR
  showing the completed upload, plus the successful `OPTIONS` + `PUT` in the network
  panel. A green test alone does not close this ticket.
- The CORS policy is committed and re-appliable from a clean checkout by one command.
- `AllowedOrigins` is explicit; `*` appears nowhere.
- A deliberately wrong origin is still rejected (verify the policy is scoped, not open).
- The failure path shows a human sentence, not "upload PUT network error".
- PR open against `Stage-11-Agentics/marquee` `main`.

data.body: Live diagnosis observed before any fix: signed speaker upload XHR from https://marquee.stage11.dev issued PUT to the R2 account endpoint with content-type=application/pdf and if-none-match=*; direct OPTIONS with Origin=https://marquee.stage11.dev, Access-Control-Request-Method=PUT, and requested headers returned HTTP 403 Forbidden with UnauthorizedCORS not configured for this bucket. The deployed portal then rendered the exact internal text upload PUT network error. c11 WKWebView network.requests reports not_supported, so its network panel cannot expose the exchange.

MRQ-92 follow-up — two things that change your work. Read both before planning.

## 1. The diagnosis is now proven, not hypothesized

I ran the probe against the real bucket just now:

    MARQUEE_R2_CORS_URL="https://<accountId>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/marquee-media/cors-probe.txt" \
      npm run check:r2-cors
    → Error: Production-origin R2 preflight failed with HTTP 403.

The `marquee-media` bucket rejects an `OPTIONS` preflight from
`https://marquee.stage11.dev` with 403. That is the whole bug. You do not need to
re-derive it — though do re-run the probe yourself so you have a live before/after.
The account ID is in `~/Projects/Stage11/code/platform/.credentials/.env` as
`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`; source it in your shell, never print it, never commit it.

## 2. The check you were asked to write already exists

`scripts/checks/check-r2-cors.mjs`, wired up as `npm run check:r2-cors`. It already
asserts everything my ticket asked for: preflight from the production origin,
`PUT` in allow-methods, `content-type` and `if-none-match` in allow-headers, and
a deliberately-wrong origin being rejected. **Do not rewrite it.** Someone
anticipated this failure and the check was simply never satisfied.

So your job narrows to:

- **Apply the CORS policy to the bucket** so the existing check passes. This is the
  actual fix and it is infrastructure, not code.
- **Commit the policy + an idempotent apply script**, so the rule survives a bucket
  rebuild and is reviewable. It exists nowhere in the repo today.
- **Wire `check:r2-cors` into the deploy path** so this cannot silently regress —
  see `DEPLOY.md`'s "After a deploy" section, which is where it belongs. It needs
  `MARQUEE_R2_CORS_URL`, which is why it never ran; make that resolvable.
- **Fix the speaker-facing error copy** ("upload PUT network error" → a plain
  sentence), per the original ticket.

## On the no-deploy rule I just sent you

That rule is about **shipping Worker code**, and it still binds — do not
`wrangler deploy`. Applying a CORS policy to the R2 bucket is different: it is the
fix itself, it is additive, it cannot ship half-finished code, and the upload path
is already 100% broken so there is no working state to regress. **You are
authorized to apply it to the real bucket.** Report exactly what you applied.

One caveat worth checking honestly: MRQ-89 replaced the Worker's R2 credential with
a bucket-scoped one. If that scoped token cannot *set* CORS rules, say so and stop
rather than quietly widening the token's permissions — that is an operator call.

## Why this was never caught

`DEPLOY.md` mentions a `LOCAL_UPLOAD_SHIM` flag. Local development shims the upload
entirely, so no local run has ever performed a real cross-origin PUT to R2. That is
the gap that let a fully-broken upload path sit behind a green suite. Worth a
sentence in your PR — and if there is a cheap way to make the shim's existence
visible to a developer, note it (do not build it in this ticket).

Updated execution contract: no Worker deploy and no live UI claim; validate the changed UI locally with c11. The operator separately authorized the infrastructure fix: re-run the existing check:r2-cors against marquee-media before applying, apply only the reviewed policy with the scoped credential from the credentials file, re-run the same check after, and report the exact result. DEPLOY.md is the authority for the post-merge deployment handoff.

data.body: VALIDATION: The existing check-r2-cors was re-run against marquee-media before the authorized mutation and failed with HTTP 403 on the production-origin OPTIONS preflight. Sourced the operator credentials file without echoing values and ran node scripts/platform/apply-r2-cors.mjs --bucket marquee-media; Wrangler exited 0. wrangler r2 bucket cors list then reported explicit origins https://marquee.stage11.dev, http://127.0.0.1:8787, http://localhost:8787; method PUT; headers content-type and if-none-match; exposed etag; max age 3600. After propagation, the unchanged check-r2-cors passed, including its deliberately wrong-origin assertion. No Worker deploy was run.\n\nLOCAL PROOF: moved the patch to /Users/atin/Projects/Stage11/deployments/Marquee-worktrees/mrq-92-r2-cors based on github/main, ran npm ci, vite build, fresh local migrations/seed, and wrangler dev on port 8793 with INSECURE_LOCAL_COOKIES=1 and LOCAL_UPLOAD_SHIM=1. c11 drove the seeded Aarush Selvan speaker portal: Presentation Upload completed with a green mark; the portal API returned status done with an attachment and the Worker log showed sign -> local PUT -> complete -> task complete. Forced one local transport error rendered the exact human sentence We couldn't upload that file. Check your connection and try again. and Retry upload. Screenshots are attached as artifacts art_01KZT1VZHMQX1GSEF6W8XDG1FP and art_01KZT1VZHH3X8Q0Z7RZZ4THG41. Local shim proof is not a real cross-origin R2 PUT; the PR states the merged Worker still needs the normal post-merge deploy. Other live portal/map observations were left to their separate tickets.

data.body:
PR opened: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/marquee/pull/46

Exact branch `mrq-92-r2-cors` is clean and pushed at `6e01a40f1701`, based on `github/main` `9e1636c3c76c`. `pr-gate --ticket MRQ-92` passed in 63.666s. The full suite passed all 499 tests; a quiet exact-head `npm test` run measured 37.608s within the 45s objective. Later reruns were also green but wall-clock slowed by concurrent sibling delegator suites (56.254s inside pr-gate, then 144.906s standalone), so that contention is recorded rather than hidden.

The real `marquee-media` policy was applied with the existing bucket-scoped credential; the apply command exited 0 and the post-propagation `check:r2-cors` passed, including wrong-origin rejection. Local c11 browser evidence is attached as validation artifacts. No Worker deploy was run; normal post-merge deployment remains.
